summary: Created a 7-phase plan to fix the lifecycle TTS defect in which every skill's Stage 8a passes an undefined $STATE_STATUS, causing lifecycle-notify.sh to hit its empty-status no-op guard and silently drop every 'Tab n researched/planned/implemented' announcement. The chosen fix direction renames the argument to the already-documented contract variable $status at the shared origin (skill-postflight-flow.md) and at all 11 inlined call sites across the core, web, cslib, and epidemiology extensions, paired with a loud-failure guard in skill_lifecycle_notify and a logged no-op branch in lifecycle-notify.sh so this silent-failure class can never again go unobserved. A narrow regression lint is in scope; the general undefined-variable linter is deferred as a follow-up. All edits target agent-system/extensions/**, followed by deploy-headless.sh and a required end-to-end verification against specs/tmp/claude-tts-notify.log rather than a grep-only check.

artifacts.summary: 7-phase plan renaming the Stage 8a lifecycle-notify argument from the undefined $STATE_STATUS to $status across 12 source-store files, adding a loud-failure guard and narrow regression lint, then deploying and verifying end-to-end.

memory_candidates.content: When a shared contract file (a lazily-imported pattern block) documents a Preconditions section naming the variables an importing file must have in scope, the contract's OWN code blocks are a drift surface that no test covers: a code block can reference a variable name absent from its own Preconditions list and nothing detects it. In this codebase that exact drift ($STATE_STATUS in a Stage 8a code block vs. the documented $status precondition) survived six-plus weeks and a full unification refactor that consolidated 11 inline copies into one shared block -- the refactor faithfully propagated the bug rather than exposing it. Two structural lessons: (1) a unification refactor validates consistency, never correctness, so it is not a review opportunity for the text it consolidates; (2) any downstream consumer with a 'no-op silently on empty/missing input' contract converts an upstream undefined-variable bug into permanent invisible failure. When planning a fix for this class, pair the rename with an observability change that makes the no-op branch loud, because the rename alone leaves the next drift equally invisible.
